briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will begin the climate briefing for August 26, 2026. Based on the 189 climate-related news items collected today, I will provide a detailed report on domestic and international climate change trends and response efforts.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Ecosystem Changes
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change are intensifying globally, including in South Korea. In the waters surrounding the Korean Peninsula, marine heatwaves have surged by 3.7 to 4 times over the past decade, with the number of occurrence days reaching 83 per year compared to the average [4, 5, 16, 22, 25, 28, 31, 32, 33]. This leads to warnings that it could exceed 300 days per year by the end of the century [28]. Climate change is also directly affecting ecosystems, blurring the wings of rainbow-colored butterflies, and causing an emergency in Jeju tangerine orchards with the emergence of a new pest, the Shandong winged planthopper [1, 12]. Internationally, the Panama Canal is under pressure from severe drought [175], record-breaking heat domes and wildfires are spreading across the southwestern United States, and London is projected to face £36 billion in losses due to climate change by 2050, revealing the global reality of the climate crisis [172, 174, 182, 187].

sections.title: 📰 Progress and Challenges in Carbon Neutrality and Climate Adaptation Legislation
sections.content: Today, significant policy progress was made in the National Assembly plenary session with the passage of amendments to the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act and the enactment of the Climate Adaptation Act, which include a 'National Greenhouse Gas Reduction Target (NDC) of 69-80% by 2040' and 'up to 90% greenhouse gas reduction by 2045' [19, 27, 34, 45, 46, 70, 83, 92, 108, 110, 116, 117, 119]. This resolves the gap in reduction targets from 2031 to 2049, making carbon reduction a legal obligation after 2030 [48, 70]. However, some criticisms have been raised regarding the 'linear reduction' method, citing burdens on future generations and constitutional issues, as well as falling short of the Constitutional Court's ruling, indicating the need for further discussion and re-amendment in the future [30, 54, 59, 98, 107, 109, 120, 170, 171]. Meanwhile, Incheon City plans to host the '2026 Air Environment Policy Forum' to address the climate crisis and improve air quality [17], and Germany is responding to criticism through its climate action commitments [177].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Future Strategies
sections.content: The South Korean government has presented a blueprint to significantly expand its renewable energy supply target to 220 GW by 2040. This is approximately six times the current scale, with a strategy to develop solar power (155 GW) and wind power (61 GW, including 45 GW offshore wind) as primary power sources [121, 124, 125, 126, 127, 129, 132, 134, 143, 145, 146, 148, 151, 152, 157, 159, 160, 163, 164, 165, 168]. The Korea Power Exchange, in collaboration with the solar and wind power industries, is preparing for the '2030 Renewable Energy 100 GW Era,' laying the groundwork across the market, grid, and industry [122, 130, 135, 138, 139, 141, 144, 147, 156, 167]. The Ministry of Climate is accelerating the decarbonization of the semiconductor supply chain by discussing renewable energy procurement solutions with global big tech companies such as Samsung, SK, Google, and ASML [137, 150, 166], and Haenam County is actively implementing guidelines for sharing renewable energy development profits to encourage local community participation [154, 158]. However, concerns are also being raised regarding the need for robust management amidst the rapid increase in renewable energy and the ability to meet surging electricity demand from sources like AI data centers [128, 133, 162, 169].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Spreading Climate Action Efforts by Local Communities and Businesses
sections.content: Various efforts by local communities and businesses to address the climate crisis are actively underway. Goyang City has opened a Climate Environment School under the theme 'The Era of Climate Crisis, Our Transition,' seeking to promote carbon neutrality practices in citizens' daily lives [2, 3, 9, 20, 21, 23, 24, 26, 69], and various local governments, including Wonju City and Busanjin-gu, are educating on resource circulation and practical daily methods through carbon neutrality academies and environmental education [36, 37, 43, 47, 49, 61, 62, 77, 79, 87, 89, 90, 94, 102, 103, 106, 111, 118]. Gangneung City is investing 372.1 billion KRW in sewage facilities to respond to climate change and increasing tourist numbers [6, 15], and GS E&C plans to research and apply 'future-oriented housing' designed for heatwaves and heavy rainfall to apartments [11]. Pulmuone, Amore, and the Climate Response Committee are strengthening public-private cooperation to spread a culture of carbon neutrality in daily life through the 'Green Benefit Campaign' [38, 39, 40, 53, 55, 58, 64, 71, 72, 75, 80, 85, 105, 114]. Asan City Council is promoting the formation of a special committee for carbon neutrality to review and improve policies [95, 96, 97, 101, 112, 113], demonstrating ongoing climate actions from various sectors.

sections.title: 🌍 International Trends in Climate Change Response
sections.content: The international community is also facing realistic challenges alongside various efforts to address climate change. Specific adaptation efforts are underway, such as a non-profit organization in Maine, USA, establishing a $20 million fund to support farmers in adapting to climate change [173]. Japan has planned to fully mobilize renewable energy and nuclear power to extend weather forecasting periods and accelerate energy independence in response to climate change [131, 184]. However, there are variations in national political responses, with criticisms raised that French politicians are showing a disconnect from the reality of the climate crisis ahead of the 2027 elections [176]. Furthermore, survey results indicating that the majority of the global public desires international cooperation in human rights, climate, and AI [188] once again underscore the importance of international collaboration to overcome the climate crisis.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis as a warning, along with various carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition efforts underway domestically and internationally, and proactive climate actions by local communities and businesses. We hope that these efforts will continue and strengthen, becoming a crucial turning point in overcoming the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
